To determine the supremum of \(\int_{Z(v)} dS\), we consider the boundary unique continuation property for harmonic functions. 

For a harmonic function \(v\) on the unit ball \(B \subset \mathbb{R}^3\) that is smooth up to the boundary, the set \(Z(v)\) consists of points on \(\partial B\) where both the Dirichlet data (\(v|_{\partial B}\)) and the Neumann data (\(\partial_\nu v|_{\partial B}\)) vanish simultaneously. By the boundary unique continuation theorem for elliptic equations on smooth domains (originating from work by F.-H. Lin and extended by Adolfsson, Escauriaza, Kenig, and others), if both the function and its normal derivative vanish on a boundary subset of positive surface measure, then \(v \equiv 0\) in \(B\).

Since \(v\) is required to be nonzero, the set \(Z(v)\) must have surface measure zero for every admissible \(v\). Consequently, \(\int_{Z(v)} dS = 0\) for every admissible \(v\), and the supremum is \(0\).

All three solutions arrive at this correct final answer of \(0\).
